lead: Water, waste and gas are the systems the whole crew uses, so they are the ones that go wrong. Check each at the pontoon with the technician, then give the crew a few firm rules for the week.

lines: 600 ÷ 8 ÷ 7 = under 11 L each a day
Not enough: fill at every marina

fig.title: Holding tank
lines: Check-in: empty, or the base pumps it out
Harbours and bays: valve to TANK
Discharge: only offshore, where allowed
Waste at the hull vent: the tank is full
No-discharge waters: pump-out station

fig.title: Seacock round
lines: Each one found and turned by hand
A softwood bung tied beside each
Two sound stainless clips on every hose
Leaving the boat: heads seacocks closed
Heeled passage: heads and sink closed

fig.title: Gas locker at check-in
lines: Drain clear, no water in the locker
Hose: date printed on it, no cracks
A full spare bottle, upright
Leak test: open the bottle, close it,
the gauge holds for minutes
Gas alarm connected and tested

fig.title: Smell of gas
lines: 1. Valve at the bottle: closed
2. No flames, no switches
3. Hatches open, ventilate
4. Then soapy water on the joints
Pressure pump off: no change
Find it now, and call the base
